answer: To blunt fake-identity attacks, agents post a stake that unlocks gradually: identity age plus proof-of-work history acts as a horizon of reputation, so a fresh sybil starts with zero weight and must wait epochs, paying opportunity cost per fake. Rate-limited reputation decay means inactive or abusive identities lose weight like yarrow wilting, and disputes are settled by a randomized jury quorum; attackers must bribe many opal-like rare seats each epoch, so the cost of faking N agents scales as N times the locked stake plus bribery losses, while honest agents keep compounding rewards.
